quote: Meanwhile, let us have a sip of tea. The afternoon glow is brightening the bamboos, the fountains are bubbling with delight, the soughing of the pines is heard in our kettle. Let us dream of evanescence, and linger in the beautiful foolishness of things.
source: Okakura Kakuzō, The Book of Tea, ch. I, The Cup of Humanity, the closing words (1906)
note: Corrected the punctuation. The 1906 text reads: let us dream of evanescence, and linger in the beautiful foolishness of things, with a comma before and. Okakura wrote the book in English, so no translator is named.
